templates: Another day survived. The tally marks are getting longer.
A crude drawing of the sun — someone still remembers what it looks like.
A row of stick figures, each labeled with a name. No one has been crossed out today.
Someone carved 'HOPE' into the concrete. Underneath, someone else added 'STILL.'
A recipe for imaginary cake. Six ingredients, all unavailable. It still made people smile.
Tally marks climb past the edge of the old paint and keep going onto the concrete.
A child drew a sun over the ventilation duct. It has too many rays. Nobody corrected it.
FOUR small handprints in charcoal, one above the other, climbing toward the ceiling.
Someone marked a patch of wall TOMATOES — SPRING. Under it, a smaller hand added a flower.
A planting plan scratched beside the door: beans by the sump, potatoes by the vent.
The repaired pipe clamp carries three sets of initials, the newest on top.
Height marks climb the door frame in pencil, name by name, the newest half a thumb taller.
The word APRIL is scratched above the bunks with a small sun under it.
A clean-water count runs down the wall in a neat column, ticked twice each week.
Someone drew a chessboard by the bunks. The current game has lasted nine days.
'SOUP AGAIN TOMORROW?' carved in a wide hand. Underneath, in different hands: 'yes', 'yes', 'if you're lucky.'
Fresh paint on the generator hatch, and a tiny flag drawn in the corner before it dried.
A birthday list, five names. Under the first, someone drew a cake with two candles.
'We take turns. Nobody freezes.' — the house rule, carved where everyone can see it.
A mural in progress: rows of sprouts labeled 'first harvest.' The watering can is bigger than the sprouts.
Tally marks — 47 days. The spacing is getting uneven.
A question scratched into the wall: 'Does anyone know what date it is?' No one has answered.
A list of names, some crossed out. The crossings are getting more frequent.
A child's drawing of the bunker. The sky above it is black, not blue.
'Miss coffee.' The handwriting is shaky. Someone else added 'miss everything.'
'FILTER 2 — CHANGE AGAIN' scratched beside the pipe, the date column half filled.
The BATTERY count by the power board: nine good, four doubtful, one that hums when it shouldn't.
Four names under NIGHT SHIFT. One is crossed out and rewritten below in a different hand.
'WHO TOOK THE WRENCH' — carved in a hurry. Underneath, smaller: 'back by six, D.'
The duty roster is carved into the wall where the paper used to hang. Wednesday's slot has three names.
The weekly water ration is chalked in a grid. Thursday was corrected twice.
'EAST HALL DRAFT' with an arrow pointing at the cracked seal, and a second arrow added later.
Someone keeps count of the bulbs that still work. The number has an arrow that only points down.
The leak above the corridor is drawn as a map now: three drips, a bucket, and a question mark.
'SWAP BUNKS AT 6' — two initials, no argument recorded.
A heat schedule in grease pencil: two hours on, one off. The 'off' hours are getting longer.
'FOOD: it's better with the pepper. Use the pepper.' — unsigned, emphatic.
Rounds marked on the door frame in pencil: morning, noon, night. Tonight's box is empty, waiting.
The generator note says 'RUN 4 HRS THEN REST — IT MEANS IT.' Two underlines for emphasis.
Someone drew a calendar grid for the month and only filled it halfway. The squares are still neat.
Just tally marks. No drawings. No words. Just lines.
A name, carved deep, then scratched out completely.
'I'm sorry' — written so small you'd miss it if you weren't looking.
A crude clock face, all hands missing. Time doesn't matter anymore.
A single word: 'WHY' — the letters growing larger and more desperate with each stroke.
A line of names stops halfway down the wall. The chalk wore out before the list did.
Twelve tally marks in a corner. Then nothing.
'DON'T SLEEP BY THE EAST DOOR.' Nobody has said why. Nobody has to.
A prayer has been rewritten so many times only the first word is still deep enough to read.
The word COLD is scratched at shoulder height, over and over, filling the plaster between two bunks.
A date is carved under a name that has been scratched away. The date is still careful.
The roster for the week has one name left on it, and the slots after that are blank.
Burial marks by the stairwell: three rows of five, then two more, unfinished.
'SORRY' cut deep enough to chip the plaster. No name after it.
A child drew a family on the wall. One figure is traced so often it has gone dark.
'IT WASN'T YOUR FAULT' — cut deep, then crossed out with one hard line.
The ration count for last week is gouged out of the wall with something not made for carving.
An arrow points at the far door above two words: 'NOT THAT ONE.' The plaster around them is cracked.
A single pair of brackets around nothing: [ ]. Nobody has filled them in. Nobody has smoothed them away.
The same short line is carved every few inches down one wall, getting shallower, then stopping.
